title: Kahn and Workflow Ordering Research Lineage
scope: Representative source-backed branches, not an exhaustive historical census or a claim of first invention.

legend.Preprint: Named research preprint; status explicitly limited
legend.Standard: Documented implementation or established form; no fabricated origin date
legend.Reference model: Study specification or competent baseline, not novelty
legend.Candidate: Proposed refinement whose exact novelty and benefit remain to be established

nodes.title: Lasser antecedent
nodes.relationship: Earlier publication cited by Kahn; not an asserted direct code derivation
nodes.change: An early published treatment of topological ordering of numbered network elements.
nodes.strength: Documents that the literature predates the named Kahn method.
nodes.limitation: Only its bibliographic role is used here; no unverified complexity or priority claim.
nodes.application: Ordering network elements.
nodes.opportunity: Use to establish historical context, not as the principal benchmark.
nodes.evidence: Bibliographic metadata and citation in Kahn; original full text not audited.

nodes.title: Kahn source removal
nodes.relationship: Kahn cites Lasser as earlier work
nodes.change: Repeatedly remove a vertex with zero remaining indegree.
nodes.strength: Standard adjacency-list implementation is linear in vertices plus edges; supports ready-set selection.
nodes.limitation: A valid order alone does not optimize retained storage or task execution time.
nodes.application: Original paper discusses PERT network analysis.
nodes.opportunity: Preserve prerequisite eligibility; change only one clearly defined additional mechanism.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: FIFO and LIFO ready sets
nodes.year: Standard forms; no origin date assigned
nodes.relationship: Ready-set implementation variants
nodes.change: Select the oldest or newest eligible vertex.
nodes.strength: Simple and inexpensive; useful controls.
nodes.limitation: Different orders can result; neither optimizes every secondary objective.
nodes.application: Sequential dependency processing.
nodes.opportunity: A queue-to-stack replacement alone is not a novel contribution.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Priority and lexicographical ordering
nodes.year: Standard forms; no origin date assigned
nodes.relationship: Changes eligible-vertex selection, not the dependency rule
nodes.change: Choose an eligible vertex by a deterministic key, commonly with a heap.
nodes.strength: Reproducibility and control over which valid order is produced.
nodes.limitation: Heap operations cost more than a FIFO queue; the quality depends on the key.
nodes.application: Deterministic task ordering and dependency tools.
nodes.opportunity: A novel, justified policy or efficient maintenance mechanism is needed beyond adding a heap.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Topological generations
nodes.year: Standard form; no origin date assigned
nodes.relationship: Groups currently eligible vertices into generations
nodes.change: Produce layers whose predecessors occur in earlier layers.
nodes.strength: Exposes dependency levels and concurrent eligibility.
nodes.limitation: Eligibility does not imply enough processors or memory; layer barriers can be restrictive.
nodes.application: Staged task execution and dependency inspection.
nodes.opportunity: Do not claim generation construction as a new parallel scheduler.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: DFS reverse postorder
nodes.relationship: Sibling static algorithm, not a Kahn extension
nodes.change: Reverse DFS completion order on a DAG.
nodes.strength: Another linear-time construction and useful independent validity reference.
nodes.limitation: Does not directly expose the same dynamic ready-set priority policy.
nodes.application: Dependency traversal and compiler graph processing.
nodes.opportunity: Use as an independent reference, not as proof that the proposed priority rule is efficient.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Enumerating topological orders
nodes.relationship: Different output problem: generate all valid orders
nodes.change: Knuth and Szwarcfiter generate multiple valid topological arrangements.
nodes.strength: Allows exact checks on very small instances.
nodes.limitation: The number of orders can be enormous.
nodes.application: Combinatorial generation and exhaustive small-case validation.
nodes.opportunity: Use tiny graphs; do not enumerate all orders of full Montage instances.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Fast generation of linear extensions
nodes.relationship: Same enumeration branch; not an assertion of direct implementation inheritance
nodes.change: Pruesse and Ruskey develop efficient generation of linear extensions.
nodes.strength: Low amortized generation work in its output model.
nodes.limitation: Explicitly writing every complete order still has an output cost; total enumeration can remain infeasible.
nodes.application: Combinatorial generation.
nodes.opportunity: Use the implementation or technique for bounded validation cases.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: AHRSZ incremental discovery
nodes.relationship: Related problem: maintain an order as dependencies change
nodes.change: Limit maintenance to an affected part instead of recomputing everything.
nodes.strength: Change-sensitive analysis motivated by computational circuits.
nodes.limitation: More involved than a static traversal; affected regions can be large.
nodes.application: Interactive semantic checking and circuit timing analysis.
nodes.opportunity: Read before claiming local repair as a new idea.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Depth-First Discovery Algorithm
nodes.relationship: Explicit refinement of Alpern discovery
nodes.change: Use depth-first discovery to reduce temporary storage.
nodes.strength: A documented example of a focused algorithmic refinement.
nodes.limitation: Still a changing-graph method; not a priority-update algorithm on a fixed DAG.
nodes.application: Incremental DAG maintenance.
nodes.opportunity: A useful model for the scale of a contribution, not a new topic by itself.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Katriel–Bodlaender online ordering
nodes.relationship: Explicit modification of the AHRSZ approach
nodes.change: Refine the earlier discovery method and its update analysis.
nodes.strength: Strengthens theoretical maintenance guarantees.
nodes.limitation: More machinery than the static algorithm; favorable graph regimes still matter.
nodes.application: Online dependency-order maintenance.
nodes.opportunity: The 2007 tight-analysis paper documents this direct parent relationship.
nodes.evidence: Relationship verified through a primary follow-up analysis and author publication metadata.

nodes.title: MNR edge-insertion maintenance
nodes.relationship: Independent milestone in the same dynamic problem
nodes.change: Maintain an existing order under edge insertions.
nodes.strength: Simple methods with O(n) amortized time per insertion in the paper’s model.
nodes.limitation: A bound across insertions differs from the cost of one static sort.
nodes.application: Dependency structures that receive new edges.
nodes.opportunity: Requires an honest edge-update dataset or explicitly controlled generated updates.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Pearce–Kelly dynamic ordering
nodes.year: 2004 conference; author lists journal version as 2007
nodes.relationship: Practical alternative to earlier incremental methods
nodes.change: Restrict searches and reassign affected vertices in the current order.
nodes.strength: Simple implementation with strong results in the authors’ experiments.
nodes.limitation: Not uniformly fastest; graph structure and affected regions matter.
nodes.application: Dynamic dependency checking, graph libraries and program analysis.
nodes.opportunity: One reassignment optimization may fit two semesters, but obtaining update traces adds work.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Batch topological maintenance
nodes.relationship: Same authors’ batch treatment of the maintenance problem
nodes.change: Process several edge insertions together and repair affected regions.
nodes.strength: Amortizes overlapping work when batches are sufficiently large.
nodes.limitation: Less attractive for tiny batches; batch construction affects results.
nodes.application: Batched dependency changes.
nodes.opportunity: Only a new batch decision or repair rule could be the contribution.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Temporary-cycle tolerance
nodes.relationship: Explicit modification of Pearce–Kelly
nodes.change: Recover topological order when a graph becomes acyclic again after temporary cycles.
nodes.strength: Supports editing situations where cycles may arise temporarily.
nodes.limitation: A cyclic graph still has no valid topological order.
nodes.application: Dependency graph editing.
nodes.opportunity: Temporary-cycle handling itself is already studied.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Ajwani–Friedrich–Meyer dense-graph ordering
nodes.relationship: Alternative dense-graph algorithm improving the prior bound; not claimed to inherit its implementation
nodes.change: Maintain an order with O(n^2.75) total time over insertions in the stated model.
nodes.strength: A historical improvement for dense graphs, with experimental comparisons.
nodes.limitation: Later bounds supersede the historical guarantee; this is total insertion cost, not static-sort runtime.
nodes.application: Dense evolving DAGs.
nodes.opportunity: Use to understand how assumptions determine which improvement matters.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Improved total insertion bounds
nodes.relationship: Chronological theory branch, not a single parent-to-child chain
nodes.change: Haeupler et al. 2012; Bender et al. 2016; Bernstein–Chechik 2018; Bhattacharya–Kulkarni 2020 improve maintenance bounds in different regimes.
nodes.strength: Strong amortized or expected guarantees for growing graphs.
nodes.limitation: Search structures and proofs are considerably more involved; graph density and randomization assumptions differ.
nodes.application: Large dynamically growing dependency graphs.
nodes.opportunity: Do not compare a total insertion bound with one static Kahn run.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Topological ordering with predictions
nodes.relationship: Uses algorithms-with-predictions for incremental ordering
nodes.change: Exploit predictions of evolving graph information while controlling prediction error.
nodes.strength: Theory addresses consistency, robustness and smooth degradation.
nodes.limitation: Adds prediction assumptions and a larger experimental burden.
nodes.application: Incremental dependency graphs with useful prior information.
nodes.opportunity: Not needed for a CPU-only fixed-workflow priority-maintenance thesis.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Strong components with predictions
nodes.relationship: Related predictive dynamic-graph branch; different maintained object
nodes.change: Maintain strongly connected components under edge insertions.
nodes.strength: Extends predictive dynamic-graph research to component structure.
nodes.limitation: Not a direct replacement for Kahn and not the same output problem.
nodes.application: Dynamic directed graphs that may contain cycles.
nodes.opportunity: Use to mark the boundary of recent related work.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Parallel topological sorting
nodes.relationship: Different machine model
nodes.change: Distribute topological-order computation across processing resources.
nodes.strength: Potential wall-clock gains when graph structure exposes parallelism.
nodes.limitation: Synchronization and dependency depth constrain benefit.
nodes.application: Parallel network analysis.
nodes.opportunity: No need for this branch when targeting one CPU process.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: External-memory topological sorting
nodes.relationship: Different cost model: block transfers
nodes.change: Cao et al. optimize input-output costs for topological sorting and related directed-graph problems.
nodes.strength: Addresses graphs that are expensive to process with ordinary memory access patterns.
nodes.limitation: A storage-transfer bound is not an ordinary CPU-operation bound.
nodes.application: Graphs larger than practical internal-memory capacity.
nodes.opportunity: A separate research project; unnecessary for the selected modest traces.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Parameterized streaming sorting
nodes.relationship: Limited-memory, multi-pass graph input model
nodes.change: Exploit graph parameters to trade stream passes against memory.
nodes.strength: Addresses constrained input access with formal bounds.
nodes.limitation: Different assumptions and proof burden from an in-memory scheduler.
nodes.application: Graph streams, with applications to SCC and 2-SAT.
nodes.opportunity: Do not add streaming merely to make the title appear newer.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Tree pebbling for memory use
nodes.relationship: Related objective: choose an execution order with low memory
nodes.change: Liu uses tree structure to optimize traversal memory.
nodes.strength: Exact structural reasoning for tree-shaped computation.
nodes.limitation: Tree-specific reasoning does not directly solve arbitrary DAGs.
nodes.application: Sparse matrix factorization.
nodes.opportunity: Establishes the history of order-dependent memory use.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Series-parallel peak-memory scheduling
nodes.relationship: Explicit extension of Liu’s tree approach
nodes.change: Extend polynomial optimization to series-parallel task graphs under the paper’s model.
nodes.strength: Exact results on a broader structured graph class.
nodes.limitation: Cannot assume arbitrary Montage graphs or shared-file semantics match this model.
nodes.application: Structured scientific computations.
nodes.opportunity: Useful theory, but reproducing the complete proof is not required for the chosen thesis.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Sequential dataflow scheduling
nodes.relationship: Extends the studied graph classes using transformations and search
nodes.change: Fradet, Girault and Honorat combine task-graph transformations and branch-and-bound.
nodes.strength: Exact optimization on suitable small or reducible graphs.
nodes.limitation: Search and conversion may grow; optimal scheduling differs from faster maintenance of one fixed heuristic.
nodes.application: Embedded dataflow applications and task graphs.
nodes.opportunity: Existing reductions must be reviewed before claiming a new scheduling reduction.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Graph transformations for peak memory
nodes.relationship: Same authors’ expanded transformation-based treatment
nodes.change: Four transformations preserve minimal peak memory; search handles unreduced cases.
nodes.strength: Formal preservation properties provide strong correctness foundations.
nodes.limitation: An optimal-memory result is not equivalence to the proposed greedy order.
nodes.application: Task graphs and synchronous dataflow programs.
nodes.opportunity: Review reduction semantics and distinguish graph transformation from metadata reduction.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: HEFT heterogeneous scheduling
nodes.relationship: Related list-scheduling problem, not Kahn genealogy
nodes.change: Rank tasks and assign them to heterogeneous processors.
nodes.strength: Balances precedence and predicted finish times at modest heuristic complexity.
nodes.limitation: Requires processor and cost assumptions; does not optimize just order-construction overhead.
nodes.application: Heterogeneous computing.
nodes.opportunity: HEFT is context, not the main baseline for identical-policy maintenance.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Memory-aware adaptive HEFT variant
nodes.relationship: Explicit HEFT variant with additional resource concerns
nodes.change: Incorporate memory limits, evictions and adaptation to observed task parameters.
nodes.strength: Targets memory failures and execution makespan jointly.
nodes.limitation: Several resource dimensions and runtime integration enlarge scope.
nodes.application: Scientific workflows on heterogeneous platforms.
nodes.opportunity: Do not replicate the whole scheduler for this undergraduate topic.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Dask memory-conscious ordering
nodes.year: Official documentation; no invention date assigned
nodes.relationship: Related practical system, not a proven direct Kahn descendant
nodes.change: Use graph structure and task-completion state to select practical execution order.
nodes.strength: Existing implementations show that ordering and bookkeeping matter.
nodes.limitation: No universal optimum for the proposed file-byte score; policies and software versions must be pinned.
nodes.application: Local and distributed data-processing task graphs.
nodes.opportunity: Inspect implementation mechanisms; benchmark fairly only under matching semantics.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Least Reference Count caching
nodes.relationship: Related use of unfinished-dependent counts; cache replacement, not task ordering
nodes.change: Count dependent computations not yet finished and use the count for cache decisions.
nodes.strength: Demonstrates dependency-aware reference tracking in data analytics.
nodes.limitation: Its objective is retaining or evicting blocks, not choosing the next ready task.
nodes.application: Spark-style data-analytics caches.
nodes.opportunity: Rules out claiming that unfinished-consumer counting alone is new.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Pegasus workflow file cleanup
nodes.year: Official documentation; no invention date assigned
nodes.relationship: Application context for file-lifetime handling
nodes.change: Arrange cleanup of data no longer needed by workflow execution.
nodes.strength: Real workflow-management need and existing implementation practice.
nodes.limitation: Per-file planning can introduce overhead; production constraints exceed the proposed simulator.
nodes.application: Scientific workflow data management.
nodes.opportunity: Do not claim to invent deletion after final use.
nodes.evidence: Publisher or author abstract and official documentation; not a full proof audit.

nodes.title: Defined storage-priority Kahn reference
nodes.relationship: Combines Kahn eligibility with a declared greedy file-byte score
nodes.change: For ready v, priority equals releasable generated-file bytes minus its original output bytes.
nodes.strength: Simple specification permits exact equivalence tests.
nodes.limitation: The score is a heuristic, not an optimal-memory guarantee; full recomputation is a correctness oracle, not a strong runtime baseline.
nodes.application: Sequential ordering of recorded Montage workflows.
nodes.opportunity: The research changes maintenance cost, not the scoring objective.
nodes.evidence: Defined model for this proposal, not a newly discovered published algorithm.

nodes.title: Efficient per-file priority maintenance
nodes.relationship: Reference implementation improvement
nodes.change: Use incremental counters, initialize singleton release credits, and batch heap refreshes by affected task.
nodes.strength: Avoids full ready-set rescoring with straightforward bookkeeping.
nodes.limitation: Still updates separate counters for files whose state may be redundant.
nodes.application: Same fixed Montage application and score.
nodes.opportunity: This is the competent baseline the candidate must beat.
nodes.evidence: Constructed benchmark baseline from standard techniques; no novelty claim.

nodes.title: Equal consumer-set aggregation
nodes.relationship: Proposed exact representation reduction
nodes.change: Share a counter across files with identical consumer sets; sum release bytes but retain original producer costs.
nodes.strength: Counter-state equality is direct to prove; may reduce repeated decrements.
nodes.limitation: Grouping has a cost; generic aggregation is old; dependency-forced final consumers can be a stronger simplification.
nodes.application: Montage files with repeated consumer sets.
nodes.opportunity: Compare against a baseline that already exploits simple forced final consumers. Do not claim fewer heap refreshes automatically.
nodes.evidence: Derived candidate and prior synthetic evidence in the separate validation package; no real Montage timing or novelty proof.

nodes.title: Static credit for a forced final consumer
nodes.relationship: Precedence-based exact specialization
nodes.change: When all other consumers precede one consumer, assign its release credit statically and remove the dynamic counter.
nodes.strength: Can remove all dynamic reference-count work for that file.
nodes.limitation: Checking the condition costs work; arbitrary consumer sets need not have a forced final consumer.
nodes.application: Files whose consumers have a dependency-determined last use.
nodes.opportunity: Include this simpler method before approving more elaborate aggregation.
nodes.evidence: Mathematical observation in this proposal; historical novelty not asserted.

nodes.title: Precedence pruning of consumer sets
nodes.relationship: Proposed generalization of forced-final-consumer recognition
nodes.change: Track only consumers with no later consumer reachable through dependencies; fold a singleton into static release credit.
nodes.strength: A short ready-task equivalence argument can justify fewer tracked consumers.
nodes.limitation: Reachability preprocessing may cost more than the updates removed; exact prior-art search remains necessary.
nodes.application: Fixed Montage file-consumption graphs.
nodes.opportunity: Keep task edges and actual file uses unchanged. Choose this OR aggregation as the thesis contribution, not both.
nodes.evidence: New derivation offered for investigation; not claimed as a first publication, tested implementation or measured improvement.

nodes.title: Adaptive sorting versus scanning in reassignment
nodes.relationship: Modifies a Pearce–Kelly subroutine rather than the Montage proposal
nodes.change: Recover affected vertices in prior order by sorting k vertices or scanning an interval of length L.
nodes.strength: Can compare O(k log(k+1)) work with O(L) while preserving reassignment.
nodes.limitation: Same optimization may exist; the study requires credible edge-update traces.
nodes.application: Build-dependency order maintenance.
nodes.opportunity: Use only if the students prefer dynamic graph algorithms and can build the update corpus early.
nodes.evidence: Derived candidate; prior-art and application-level performance unresolved.

benchmark.application: Montage 2MASS, fixed workflow, one simulated task completes at a time
metrics: Total ordering time including method-specific initialization and reduction
benchmark.correctness: Every dependency respected; exact reference priority and task-order equivalence with identical tie-breaking.
baselines: Strongest simple forced-final-consumer or aggregation reference for the chosen candidate
caveats: No actual image processing, GPU, retries, new edge arrivals or distributed execution.
File sizes are not process RAM measurements.
Repeated timings are not additional independent workflow instances.
The exact novelty and real Montage runtime advantage remain unverified.
Do not transform a held-out workflow after viewing its results.

roadmap: Reproduce the competent baseline, freeze file semantics, audit the two development traces.
Working loader, dependency validator, source comparison table.
Evaluate ONE reduction against the strongest simple alternative.
Equivalence proof, operation count and pilot including preprocessing.
Resolve the closest prior work and freeze the method and test plan.
Approved narrow contribution, pseudocode, versioned code and six held-out files.
Run paired measurements and automated correctness checks.
Reproducible logs for three methods across six evaluation instances.
Explain successes, regressions and preprocessing break-even.
Per-instance timing and dynamic-counter-update results; no inflated independence claims.
Write, review and reproduce the final study.
Thesis, code, benchmark manifests, proof, limitations and defense material.
